prompt:
Implement the incremental graph compiler and migrate all sixteen product build frontends in this dependency-free TypeScript monorepo. Node's type stripping is available; use erasable TypeScript and explicit .ts import extensions. Add public regression tests.

Public API in src/graph.ts:
- NodeSpec = {id:string, deps:string[], kind:'input'|'sum'|'product'|'offset', value?:number}; Graph exposes constructor(nodes:NodeSpec[]), evaluate(targets:string[], inputs:Record<string,number>): {values:Record<string,number>, executed:string[]}, replace(nodes:NodeSpec[]):void, snapshot():NodeSpec[].
- IDs/dependencies are nonempty strings. IDs are unique; dependency IDs must exist; duplicate dependencies, self references and ANY cycle (even outside requested targets) are invalid. input has no dependencies and no value; sum/product have at least one dependency and no value; offset has exactly one dependency and a finite numeric value. Reject bad node shapes/extra properties with Error. Constructor and replace validate the entire graph before installing it. replace failure preserves the old graph AND cache. snapshot is sorted by id and deep-owned.
- evaluate computes only the transitive closure of targets. Targets may repeat; unknown target throws. Only reached input nodes need values; each must be an own property of inputs containing a finite number. Unrelated inputs are ignored. Sum/product combine deps in their declared order; offset adds its value. Reject nonfinite results. A failed evaluate changes neither the cache nor the prior graph.
- Cache is per Graph instance and keyed by node id plus its exact spec and ordered dependency result values (input nodes use their supplied numeric value). A cached node is not executed. On a successful evaluate, executed lists the cache misses in deterministic depth-first postorder: visit targets in caller order, deps in declared order, each node once. values contains ONLY requested target ids (duplicate targets collapse). Return fresh data. Replacing with an equivalent graph preserves all entries. On replace, invalidate every changed/added/removed node and all of its transitive dependents; unchanged independent entries survive. Changing only input values on evaluate invalidates through dependency result values, so unchanged intermediate results allow downstream cache hits. Do not use time, randomness or global caches.

Integration contract:
- Each products/<product>/schema.ts exports its own wire field names and numeric factor. Keep these. compile(raw) in each compiler.ts converts an array of that product's wire nodes into NodeSpec[]: wire ID/deps/kind/amount fields map to id/deps/kind/value (omit value when the amount field is absent), then validate with Graph. Missing or malformed wire shapes throw Error. Do not coerce numeric strings. Unknown wire keys may be ignored. No input mutation.
- Each frontend.ts exposes create(raw) -> Frontend with run(targets,inputs), update(raw), inspect(). These delegate to ONE persistent Graph so cache survives calls and successful equivalent updates. inspect() returns Graph.snapshot(). src/api.ts exports products (all sixteen names), create(product,raw) and rejects unknown product. Keep the old summarize(product,raw,targets,inputs) wrapper and make it return the target numeric values, using the new semantics.
- Existing product fixtures and tests cover legacy input/sum only. Complete product/offset support, all validation, incremental replacement, atomic failure, ownership and every product boundary. Product factors are used by the existing legacy fixture generator only, not an extra runtime multiplier.
